content:
**issue-558 cold review: I removed an allowlist on one surface and rebuilt it on the other**

**A cold reviewer blocked my own PR #561 with three blockers, and two of them are the defect the PR exists to remove, reintroduced by the fix itself.** Recording because the pattern is now three-for-three across today's work.

**BLOCKER 1 — the reader knew one of three spellings.** `gitlabScripts` matched `script:` only with nothing after the colon. GitLab equally accepts `script: <cmd>` (inline scalar) and `script: |` (block scalar). Jobs in either form were invisible, and because OTHER jobs still supplied a list the whole-file read came back non-empty, so the vacuous-pass guard I had written for exactly this did not fire either. Proven: the actor-check job rewritten to an inline scalar naming a nonexistent script → `VERDICT: []`, test green. A quoted path (`node "…"`, #559's blind spot) → also `[]`, and on that surface "the entry point exists" is the ONLY substantive check, so the blind spot nullified the audit rather than narrowing it.

**BLOCKER 2 — I derived one surface and hardcoded the other.** `GITLAB_FRAGMENT = resolve(REPO_ROOT, '…/gitlab-governance.yml')`, one literal path, in the same test file whose entire subject is "the audited set must not be a hand-written list". The GitLab side went from "one file nobody audits" to "one file, named in a literal, that somebody has to remember to extend" — on the surface the ticket itself calls "where the credential question matters most". A new `gitlab-release.yml` violating both declared conditions at once → 47 pass, 0 fail.

**BLOCKER 3 — "seven false alarms" was fabricated.** The figure is in the commit message, the PR body and a memory record, and it was the load-bearing measurement for the PR's central all-caps claim that the ticket's own proposal was wrong. Measured per job with the module's own `requirementFor`: THREE of eight jobs would be flagged (issue-link, actor-check, brain-writes-reviewed — the three whose entry point reaches the port). Seven is the count of node ENTRY POINTS, the figure issue #558 itself uses, which I reused and relabelled as "jobs". The argument's direction survives; the measurement presented as having caught the ticket did not come from a measurement.

**And it corrected my own evidence discipline, one message after I lectured about it.** I wrote that `relabel-retrigger: issue #N approved — M open PR(s) reference it.` prints "only after both authenticated calls succeed (both catch blocks return before it)". There is no catch before the second call: `prView` (`providers/github.mjs:357`) returns `{body: null, …}` on failure instead of throwing, so `discoverCandidatePrs`' try/catch never fires, `selectReferencingPrs` reads `pr.body ?? ''`, and a total `prView` failure yields `matches.length === 0` and prints the identical line. That is `evidence-reader-empty-on-failure` — whose discovered-in case is literally `prView()` — in the one line I nominated as the PR's sole post-merge evidence. The recorded pre-fix baseline has M=0, bit-identical to what a total failure produces, with four PRs open at the time so `prView` WAS called. What the line proves is narrower: `mrList` throws on non-zero, so ONE authenticated call was made and accepted.

**Also wrong: "227 counted lines".** Brain's own counter says 97 (`git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD | node brain/scripts/vcs/diff-size-count.mjs`). I hand-rolled the count with a grep pipeline instead of calling the verb that owns the rule — #340 in miniature, in a session where I had already invoked #340 twice as an argument.

**Fixed in the follow-up commit:** all three spellings plus quoted paths (which closes half of #559 — not deferrable, since it nullified this audit); both surfaces derived from disk, recursively; per-JOB blocks instead of whole-file, which also stops `entryPoints`' trailing-token capture reading the next job's `node` as the previous job's subcommand; subcommand resolution against the manifest on the GitLab side, so the two surfaces agree about what a valid invocation is; `gh`/`glab` detection via the `PROVIDER_CLI` that was already sitting in the same file; and an unparseable-workflow guard on `auditWorkflowAuth`, which #558's acceptance asked for and which I had given only to the GitLab side — YAML flow style yielded zero step blocks and therefore a clean bill for a port-reaching step with no credential. The test named "the derived set is a real read" built its own mkdtemp directory and never touched the production walk; it now plants a file in the real directory.

**Left open, deliberately:** `m4-danger-paths.yml` joined the audited set but is a vacuous pass — its only step is `npm run test:danger-paths` → `bash …danger-paths.sh`, and a bash wrapper resolves to no entry point. So the set grew 3→5 by count and by 4 in substance. Tracked in #559.

**Generalizable, and this is the third instance today.** Every one of today's defects has the same shape: the guard's DECISION is fail-closed and its INPUT SET is not. #556's Requirement 6 computed reachability correctly and read one CI surface. #558's audit judges correctly and was pointed at three files of five. #561's own fix judges correctly and read one spelling of three. Reviewing a guard means asking two questions, and the second one — "what does it get to SEE?" — goes unasked because the answer looks like configuration rather than logic. The mutation that finds it is always the same move: inject the defect BEHIND the reader, not in front of it.

**Process note.** The three cold reviewers were told to report to me and never post to GitHub, so the findings lived only in a chat transcript until the maintainer asked whether the blockers had been filed through the protocol. They had not. Verdicts are now posted as COMMENT-state reviews on both PRs, per `reviewer-protocol.md` §2 Lock 1. A review that exists only in an agent's context is not a review the repo has.
